summary:
Astro-Salud: Crew Health for Spaceflight

We developed Astro-Salud, a web app for monitoring astronaut health and supporting crew wellness during human spaceflight. It gives mission teams a single place to track the physical and mental wellbeing of the crew, even tho not completed, we plan to use sensors to make us get accurate information from the crew member.

Our project addresses a central challenge of long-duration missions. Astronauts face microgravity, radiation, isolation, and limited access to medical care, and as missions move toward the Moon and Mars, real-time support from Earth becomes harder. With Astro-Salud, crews and flight surgeons can spot health changes early and respond before small issues become serious problems.

We believe this matters because crew health is the foundation of mission success. Early detection and proactive wellness support protect astronauts, reduce mission risk, and help make deep-space exploration safer and more sustainable.
details:
Astro-Salud is a web app that helps monitor astronaut health and crew wellness during spaceflight. It brings together physiological and behavioral health indicators, such as vitals signs, sleep, stress,unusual symptoms into one dashboard. Crew members and mission teams can track trends over time and see early warning signs this will be taken using a sensor bracelet or vest that they will wear while taking part in the mission.

Astro Salud lets crews and flight surgeons detect health changes early, before they become emergencies. It helps crews stay informed about their own wellbeing when real time medical support from Earth is delayed or limited. It also puts physical and mental health in one place instead of treating them separately.

We want to make long duration missions safer by supporting proactive health care in deep space. By catching problems early and promoting crew wellness, Astro Salud can reduce mission risk and support more sustainable exploration of the Moon and Mars. The same approach could also help remote and underserved communities on Earth where medical access is limited.

We built this web frontend using react, typescript and tailwind css for styling, github for collaboration between everyone in the team and finally deployed on Vercel.
here is our github repository: https://github.com/tankengrayan659-l/ASTRO_SALUD

We combined physical and mental wellness monitoring in a single, accessible information from the resources that was given to use.

We considered the real constraints of spaceflight: limited connectivity, delayed communication with Earth, and the need for reliable, low resource software. We also thought about usability under stress, data privacy for sensitive health information, and the mix of physical and psychological risks astronauts face, including microgravity, radiation, and isolation.
